column7: Decides whether a grant whose descriptor revision moved is fenced to ReconnectRequired (skipping unchanged, absent and revoked), so a wrong branch leaves a stale-descriptor credential live.
Draws a fresh private scratch file and skips (never overwrites) residue at a drawn name, so a mistake could write credential bytes over another writer's file.
Windows creation of the credential scratch file private with exclusive sharing, so a mistake would leave sealed token bytes readable by other principals.

Refuses an authority manifest above max_authority_bytes (the TooLarge refusal commit_grant turns into CapacityExhausted) and seals it under the configured key with bound AAD; an allow/deny decision under the 2026-10-09 guard.

Seals the token record under AAD binding instance, epoch and the account fields and builds the Connected authority entry with its version fields, so a mistake silently breaks account binding and the version fence.

Refuses a grant that would add an entry past max_entries, and maps a manifest too large for a new entry to CapacityExhausted; a global cap, but it decides allow or deny, so the 2026-10-09 guard makes it critical (as admit_active).
Debug impl that prints key IDs and names only and omits key bytes, so a mistake would silently leak custody key material into logs.
Builds the GrantRecord a 3.x token migrates into (refuses an empty access token, seeds revisions, scopes and expiry), so a mistake silently mints a grant with wrong scopes or lifetime.
Chooses the scope set attributed to a migrated grant (record, else descriptor, else refuse), which later refresh broadening checks rely on, but it does not itself enforce them.
Selects which resource URL the 3.x token file was keyed on, so a mistake migrates the wrong credential, though the bound-backend check is elsewhere.

Binds a legacy credential to a specific personal_managed descriptor and its resource and issuer (refusing absent or non-managed descriptors, opening not creating the store) before the guarded write, deciding which account identity receives the credential.

The only code that overwrites the provider tokens copied out for revocation; no other type wipes them (no zeroize or SecretString in the tree), so a no-op leaves live refresh and access tokens in freed memory.
Debug impl prints only the token count; a mistake would silently leak revoked-token secrets into logs.
Tombstones the account-keyed grant under one authority acquisition and captures its tokens, so a revoked grant is refused thereafter.
Decides whether the account holds a live grant for the given descriptor revision, treating other revisions and revoked/reconnect states as not connected.

Decides that every captured token is sent for RFC 7009 revocation even after a failure and that Confirmed is reported only when all succeed; revoke_token sends one token, so a mutant that stops early leaves the access token usable upstream while reporting confirmed.
Debug impl omits all fields; a mistake would silently leak refreshed access and refresh tokens into logs.
Debug impl omits all fields; a mistake would silently leak the released access token into logs.
Builds the non-secret prior-state snapshot the guarded consent commit compares against; a mistake would silently weaken the stale-consent fence.
Builds the GrantVersion used as the compare-and-swap expectation for refresh and fence; a mistake would silently disable the CAS.
Turns an account key into a lease or a typed refusal (offer, revoked, reconnect) based on the stored grant state.
Routes revocation to the store's single-acquisition revoke_capturing; a mistake would leave the grant live.
Builds the per-full-account-key rotation lock; a mistake would let concurrent refreshes race or accounts share a lock.
Chooses which refusal (revoked, reconnect, lease retired) to report after the CAS already refused; a mistake would misreport the refusal.
Opens the store (claiming both exclusive file locks) and builds the one service, so a mistake would silently leave custody running without its lock or service wiring.
Refuses every store call once shutdown has begun or the in-flight bound is reached, gating access to the credential store.
Routes every store operation through admit and holds its permit for the whole call, so a mistake would silently bypass the admission gate.
Calls admit itself before the provider refresh, so a mistake would silently let a refresh bypass the shutdown and bound gate.
Calls admit itself before the 401 refresh path, so a mistake would silently let it bypass the shutdown and bound gate.

Refuses the refresh provider once shutdown has taken the service out of its slot (after the drain), the same moment the RFC 7009 revocation and authorize-URL calls that need it lose it; a parallel shutdown gate beside admit.
Sets the shutting_down flag that admit enforces and drains permits before releasing the store, so a mistake would silently leave new work admitted.
Passes the principal limits and owner to the store journey creation with a checked clock, so a mistake would silently disable the journey creation limits and owner binding.
Passes the owner and limits to offer_connect_journey, so a mistake would silently disable owner-scoped reuse and the creation limits.
Passes the caller principal to journey_status_owned, so a mistake would silently disable the owner-only status scoping.
Arms the journey under the owner compare and builds the authorize URL from the sealed state and verifier on the pinned endpoint, so it binds the OAuth state and PKCE verifier to the owner.
Forwards the OAuth callback to complete_callback, so a mistake would silently route around the state, binding and exchange verification.
Calls store.start_journey with the owner and one shared now, so a mistake would silently disable the owner compare and arm deadline.
Copies the configured journey limits into JourneyLimits, so a wrong mapping would silently loosen the per-user and creation limits.

Chooses which of a revoked grant's tokens are sent for provider revocation (refresh then access, empty ones skipped); a mutant that drops one leaves that token usable upstream while the outcome reads confirmed.
